correctness.rationale: After dihedral reduction, six relative edge classes admit explicit signed-facet lower certificates L_j(d). Their pointwise minimum is the stated three-branch function M. The opposite six edges are covered because y->-y swaps the two chord lengths and M is a decreasing involution. Three explicit edge families attain M on [0,1], [1,sqrt(3)] and [sqrt(3),2]. Substitution into the finite facet representation proves the exact distance and sum norms. The angle-modulus formula is then its definition.
risks: Endpoint points lie on two closed edges, but the facet proof is nonexclusive and therefore remains valid at ties.
The symbolic certificate assumes exactly the displayed linearly isometric dodecagon normalization.

originality.rationale: The defining 2022 full text was inspected at the definitions of both angle moduli, the concrete-space examples, Proposition 7 relating the smoothness modulus to the minimum sum chord, and the conclusions; no regular-dodecagon or regular-polygon computation appears. published-finding corpus searches covered the exact invariant, dodecagon aliases, all three branch expressions, the minimum-chord equivalent formulation, and classical-modulus wording. The closest same-invariant record is the regular-octagon unit-separation value. Own ledgers were checked: the dodecagonal angle-convexity profile gives the opposite extremum, while the hexagonal smoothness profile is a different norm.

No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a full one-parameter modulus, not a single value. Its three affine chord regimes and exact transitions at 1 and sqrt(3) describe the lower boundary of the dodecagonal two-chord geometry and complement the previously known opposite maximum-chord profile. The involutive structure of the sharp lower envelope is a nontrivial geometric feature useful for other fixed-separation constants.
risks: The profile is specific to the dodecagon; a general regular-polygon law remains open here.
